name: Latte
caffeine: All of it comes from the double shot; a bigger cup tastes weaker but holds the same caffeine.

house.ask: Not printed on our menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will make a latte, and at what price.

what: A double espresso filled with steamed milk in an 8 to 12 oz cup. The milk is stretched briefly and rolled long: glossy, with about a quarter inch of foam, less air than a cappuccino and enough to hold a pattern. It is the base under nearly every flavoured coffee.
taste: Mild and sweet, milk in front and the coffee behind it; weaker in taste as the cup grows.

steps: Pull a double, 18 to 20 g in, 36 to 40 g out, into a warmed cup.
Steam 6.5 to 10.5 oz cold milk, stretched briefly, then spun glossy; cut near 135 to 140F (57 to 60C).
Tilt the cup and pour from height into the centre, so the milk mixes under the crema.
At half to two thirds full, drop the spout to the surface to float a heart or rosetta.
make.ratio: 1 part espresso to 5 or more parts milk
make.dose: 18 to 20 g coffee; 6.5 to 10.5 oz milk
make.cup: Warmed 8 to 12 oz cup or tall glass

serve: On a saucer with a teaspoon, poured to the rim, art facing the guest, sugar on the side. For extra hot, warm the cup and take the milk no further than 160F (71C).
story: Caffè latte is Italian for coffee and milk, and in Italy the single word latte brings a glass of milk, which a travelled guest enjoys hearing. The bar lesson is honesty about art: a clean rosetta proves the milk, never the shot.
guest: A double espresso with plenty of silky steamed milk and a thin foam: mild and creamy, the coffee in the background.
watch: Taste the shot before you pour: a pattern on a sour double is still a bad drink.
Past 160F (71C) the milk cooks, smells eggy and loses its sweetness; re-steaming cannot fix it.
Plant milks foam differently; send any allergy question to a manager.

study: The pour: height, flow and the wiggle

recall.answer: A double espresso in a warmed 8 to 12 oz cup, filled with milk stretched briefly and rolled long, about a quarter inch of foam, poured with a pattern. Mild and sweet, milk in front.

quiz.q: A guest at a bar in Milan asks for 'a latte'. What arrives?
quiz.explain: Latte is Italian for milk. The espresso drink is caffè latte.

quiz.q: Off one double shot, why does a 12 oz latte taste weaker than an 8 oz?
options: Hotter milk in a big cup
A thicker foam cap mutes it
quiz.explain: The shot stays the same and the milk grows, so the cup tastes milder with the same caffeine.

quiz.q: What does a clean rosetta prove about a latte?
quiz.explain: Art proves the milk was well textured, never the shot: taste the espresso first.
